projects.name: Error correction and control software for quantum computers
projects.problem: A fault-tolerant quantum computer is mostly a classical computer. It needs a decoder that catches and fixes qubit errors in real time and a compiler that targets logical qubits, and only the biggest quantum companies have teams to build them.
projects.solution: A real-time decoder for a qubit type IBM's work doesn't cover, such as neutral atoms or trapped ions, sold as FPGA IP. From there, the control stack for every quantum vendor that can't build its own.
projects.timing: DOE's $215M Quantum Competition names its first teams no earlier than November 13, 2026. DOE wants a first scientifically useful machine by 2028.
projects.one_liner: Every team trying to build a fault-tolerant quantum computer needs a classical system that catches and fixes qubit errors in real time, plus a compiler that targets logical qubits. Two people can build the first version of that today. We'd back a team that starts with one decoder for one qubit type and grows into the control layer that sits under every vendor's machine.
projects.wedge: Real-time decoder for one non-superconducting qubit type, as FPGA IP
projects.trigger: DOE Quantum (Q) Competition initial selections, no earlier than Nov 13, 2026.

projects.name: RF data and models for contested spectrum
projects.problem: Militaries and carriers are crowding into the same radio spectrum, and the models that classify signals in it lack labeled training data. A Navy topic asks for an 8-petabyte recorder because the department doesn't have the datasets.
projects.solution: A data engine that records, labels and curates radio signal data, and fine-tunes a model for each mission that runs on off-the-shelf software-defined radios.
projects.timing: The FCC plans to start auctioning 160 MHz of upper C-band on April 27, 2027, adding more shared spectrum to watch. The Army's spectrum warfare competition opens April 19.
projects.one_liner: Militaries and carriers are crowding into the same spectrum, and the models that classify signals in it are short of labeled data. A Navy topic asks for an 8-petabyte recorder because the department lacks the datasets, and the FCC plans to start auctioning 160 MHz of upper C-band in April 2027, which means more shared spectrum to monitor. We'd back the data engine that records, labels and curates RF data and fine-tunes models for each mission, and we think the winner becomes the reference spectrum layer for militaries, carriers and regulators.
projects.wedge: RF data engine that records, labels and curates I/Q data, plus a per-mission fine-tuned model that runs on COTS SDRs
projects.trigger: FCC Upper C-band Auction 115 is tentatively scheduled to begin Apr 27, 2027 (FCC DA 26-769). The Army's xTech Spectrum Enabled Warfare competition (ARM27BX01-DP001) runs Apr 19 to May 7, 2027 (DSIP).

projects.name: Recovering technical data for aging weapons
projects.problem: The military keeps weapons in service for decades after the drawings, manuals and code behind them have gone stale. Without usable data, it can't bring in a new supplier to make a replacement part.
projects.solution: Software that turns scanned drawings, parts lists and old manuals into a validated 3D model and a technical data package a supplier can build from, flagging gaps and data-rights markings. Every long-lived machine has the same problem.
projects.timing: The Air Force, Navy and DLA have posted 16 small-business topics asking for this since FY25. Two Air Force topics close November 25, 2026.
projects.one_liner: The military keeps weapons in service for decades after the drawings, manuals and code behind them have gone stale, and it can't re-source a part it has no usable data for. The Air Force, Navy and DLA have posted 16 small-business topics since FY25 asking for software that turns scanned drawings and old manuals into models a supplier can build from. We'd back that software, and we think the winner becomes the system of record for the aftermarket of every long-lived machine.
projects.wedge: Scanned drawings, BOMs and manuals to a validated 3D model and model-based technical data package, with gaps and data-rights markings flagged
projects.trigger: Air Force SBIR topics DAF27BZ01-DV008 (technical data package modernization) and DAF27BZ01-DV012 (autonomous technical data package to robotic task spec) close Nov 25, 2026 at 9:00 AM PT (DSIP).

projects.name: Licensing and safety software for microreactors
projects.problem: Microreactor makers now answer to more than one regulator while their designs are still changing. The NRC's new rule for advanced reactors puts probabilistic risk assessment at the center of every application, and the Army will regulate the reactors it buys itself.
projects.solution: A digital twin that keeps one microreactor design's risk assessment and licensing basis current as the design changes, built for both the NRC and the Army. It can grow into the licensing and operations system for small reactors.
projects.timing: The Army has awarded up to $2.2B to five microreactor makers and wants the first one running by September 2028. DOE's fall small-business program includes a reactor digital twin topic, with first pitches due December 16, 2026.
projects.one_liner: The NRC's new licensing rule for advanced reactors, Part 53, is now final and puts probabilistic risk assessment at the center of every application. The Army has awarded up to $2.2B to five microreactor makers, will regulate those reactors itself rather than through the NRC, and wants the first one running by September 2028. Every vendor now has to keep a safety case current for more than one regulator while its design is still changing. We'd back the digital twin that keeps that safety case current, and we think the winner becomes the licensing and operations system for small reactors.
projects.wedge: Living PRA and licensing-basis digital twin for one microreactor design, built for Part 53 and the Army's review
projects.trigger: First-stage pitches due for DOE's Fall 2026 SBIR/STTR Phase I opportunity, which includes a topic on reactor digital twins aimed at shortening licensing (DOE Office of Technology Commercialization, via ConnectWerx).

projects.name: Risk underwriting for next-generation geothermal
projects.problem: Every enhanced geothermal project has to convince a lender that its wells will keep producing for decades. Lenders and insurers have no independent way to price that risk yet.
projects.solution: A model of well performance and decline for geothermal projects, sold to lenders and insurers. If its forecasts hold up, it becomes the underwriting standard for energy below ground.
projects.timing: Fervo went public in May 2026 and brought its first commercial plant online in September, financed with non-recourse debt. More of that plant comes online in early 2027, and every project behind it will need financing.
projects.one_liner: Enhanced geothermal went from pilot to public company this year: Fervo listed in May and its first commercial plant came online in September, with non-recourse debt behind it and a 396 MW contract with Google. Every project after it has to convince a lender that its wells will keep producing for decades. We'd back the independent model that prices that subsurface risk, and we think the winner becomes the underwriting standard for energy below ground.
projects.wedge: Well-performance and decline model for EGS projects, sold to lenders and insurers
projects.trigger: Fervo's Cape Station Phase I reaches about 100 MW, with GeoBlocks 2 and 3 expected to reach initial power in Q1 2027 (Fervo Q2 2026 results).

projects.name: Evidence and filings for on-demand gene editing
projects.problem: In February 2026 the FDA proposed approving gene editors based on how they work, so one editor could cover many mutations and new ones could be added without a new trial. Each new patient then becomes a small filing, and most of this work happens in academic labs with small teams.
projects.solution: Software that builds the evidence package for each new mutation. If on-demand gene editing scales, every patient's filing runs through a system like this.
projects.timing: Penn and CHOP's umbrella trial for seven urea cycle disorders can start once all seven investigational new drug applications are in place, which the team expects in 2027.
projects.one_liner: In February the FDA proposed approving gene editors on mechanism: one editor can cover many mutations, and new mutations could be added without a new trial. That turns each new patient into a small, repeated filing, and nearly all of this work still sits in academic labs with small teams. We'd back the software that builds those filings, and we think the winner becomes the system on-demand genetic medicine runs on.
projects.wedge: Per-variant evidence package for plausible-mechanism filings
projects.trigger: Penn and CHOP's umbrella trial for seven urea cycle disorders can begin once all seven INDs are in place, which the team expects in 2027 (Aldevron, Jun 2026).

projects.name: Power systems for robots on solid-state batteries
projects.problem: Humanoid robots need long runtime and can pay a premium for batteries, which makes them a likely first market for solid-state cells. Robot makers will have to qualify these cells with no agreed test standard, in packs that change with every redesign.
projects.solution: Cell qualification and battery management for humanoid makers moving to solid-state cells, with a safety file that buyers accept. From there, the power system for robots.
projects.timing: Samsung SDI plans to start mass production in the second half of 2027, with humanoid robots as the likely first application. Chinese cell makers are already shipping samples to robot companies.
projects.one_liner: Solid-state batteries keep slipping in cars, but humanoid robots can pay the premium and need the runtime. Samsung SDI plans to mass-produce them with humanoids as the first application in the second half of 2027, and Chinese cell makers are already shipping robot samples. Robot makers will be qualifying new cells with no agreed test standard, in packs that change with every redesign. We'd back the qualification and battery-management layer they need, and we think the winner grows into the power system for robots.
projects.wedge: Cell qualification and BMS for humanoid makers adopting solid-state cells, with a safety file buyers accept
projects.trigger: Samsung SDI begins mass production of all-solid-state batteries in the second half of 2027, with humanoid robots as the likely first application (Herald Corporation).

projects.name: The toolchain for designed biology
projects.problem: Designing a protein or a cell with a model is getting cheap. Making it is not. Every designed sequence has to clear screening before a supplier will synthesize the DNA, and in California that check is becoming law.
projects.solution: Software that takes a designed construct, clears it, orders it and keeps a signed record of what was designed, cleared and made. Sold to teams that design sequences with models.
projects.timing: California's gene synthesis law makes screening a legal condition of selling synthetic DNA from January 1, 2027, and tighter rules apply from October 13, 2027.
projects.one_liner: Designing a protein or a cell is getting cheap. Making it, clearing it and finding out whether it works is not. California's gene synthesis law puts a dated, penalised gate between a designed sequence and physical DNA from Jan 1, 2027, and the tighter screening rules bite there from Oct 13, 2027. We'd back the software that sits at that gate: the step that takes a designed construct, clears it, gets it made and records what happened.
projects.wedge: Pre-synthesis clearance and ordering software sold to teams that design sequences with models, with a signed record of what was designed, cleared and made
projects.trigger: California AB 1864 (Chapter 852, Statutes of 2026) makes adherence to the federal nucleic acid synthesis screening framework a legal condition of producing or selling synthetic DNA in California. The chapter takes effect Jan 1, 2027, and the tighter framework provisions apply in the state from Oct 13, 2027 (Health and Safety Code 24201(d)).

projects.name: Seafloor monitoring for deep-sea mining and undersea infrastructure
projects.problem: The US is close to deciding its first commercial deep-sea mining permit, and the regulator can make ongoing seafloor monitoring a condition of it. Undersea cable owners now have to certify physical security plans too. Today, watching the deep seafloor takes a research ship.
projects.solution: Software that turns data from low-cost seafloor sensors into the plume and impact reports a mining permit will require. Cable owners, offshore wind and navies need the same picture of the seafloor.
projects.timing: The Metals Company expects NOAA to decide on its permit by the end of March 2027.
projects.one_liner: The US is close to deciding its first commercial deep-sea mining permit, and the seafloor is filling up with cables that now carry security rules. Every one of those activities will need someone to watch the seafloor continuously, and today that takes a research ship. We'd back the software that turns cheap seafloor sensors into monitoring a regulator accepts.
projects.wedge: Plume and impact analytics for mining permit conditions
projects.trigger: NOAA's decision on The Metals Company USA's consolidated exploration license and commercial recovery permit, which TMC projects before the end of Q1 2027.

projects.name: Autonomy for low-cost military drones
projects.problem: The Pentagon plans to buy more than 200,000 small attack drones by 2027 and treats them as consumables. The airframes are getting cheap. Software that still finds and hits a target when GPS and radio links are jammed is scarce.
projects.solution: A navigation and terminal guidance module that drone makers drop in to pass the program's tests, priced for drones that cost a few thousand dollars. Most of the companies competing for orders would rather buy this than build it.
projects.timing: The Drone Dominance Program buys in rounds, with a fly-off before each large order. The next one, Gauntlet 3, is expected around February 2027.
projects.one_liner: The Pentagon plans to buy more than 200,000 small attack drones by 2027 through a series of fly-off competitions. The airframes are getting cheap. What will be scarce is software that still finds and hits a target when GPS and radio links are jammed. We'd back that software, sold to every drone maker in the competition.
projects.wedge: Visual navigation and terminal guidance module for drone makers
projects.trigger: Drone Dominance Program Gauntlet 3, which the program schedules about six months after Gauntlet 2 (held Aug 2026).

projects.name: Software for orbital data centers
projects.problem: The first data center satellites are about to go into service. Radiation corrupts computation in orbit, and the link to the ground can only carry so much data.
projects.solution: An inference runtime that tolerates radiation, plus software that decides what to process in orbit and what to send down. The goal is to run the orbital cloud without building the satellites.
projects.timing: Starcloud-2 aims to be fully operational in orbit in 2027.
projects.one_liner: The first data center satellites aim to be fully operational in 2027. They need inference software that tolerates radiation and a way to decide what to send to the ground. We'd back that software, and we think the winner can become the company that runs the orbital cloud without building the satellites.
projects.wedge: Radiation-tolerant inference runtime for orbital compute
projects.trigger: Starcloud-2 fully operational in sun-synchronous orbit.

projects.name: Yield and process control for new fabs
projects.problem: New companies are building chip fabs and lithography in the US for the first time in a generation. A new process starts with no production history, so there is very little data to learn its defects from.
projects.solution: Defect classification that works from small amounts of data, sold to new fabs. The company that learns the new process first can grow into its inspection and metrology supplier, the way KLA did for the last one.
projects.timing: Substrate says its US foundry will be running wafers by 2028.
projects.one_liner: New companies are trying to build fabs and lithography in the US for the first time in a generation. A new process needs new ways to measure and fix it. We'd back yield software for those fabs, and we think the winner can grow into the inspection and metrology company for the new process, the way KLA did for the last one.
projects.wedge: Small-data defect classification for new fabs
projects.trigger: Substrate says its US foundry will run wafers by 2028.

projects.name: Software for running lab instruments with AI
projects.problem: AI models can propose experiments far faster than people can run them. Beamlines, microscopes and liquid handlers were built for human operators, and connecting an agent to one safely means new drivers, control loops and interlocks for each instrument.
projects.solution: Software that lets an agent run one class of instrument at DOE facilities in a closed loop, with interlocks a facility safety officer will sign off on and a record of every experiment the AI chose. That record gets more valuable as more R&D runs this way.
projects.timing: DOE's Genesis Mission is paying national-lab facilities to run AI-driven experiments. Phase II applications are due December 17, 2026.
projects.one_liner: DOE's Genesis Mission pays national-lab facilities to run AI-driven experiments, and those facilities need software that lets an agent drive existing instruments safely. We'd back that control layer, and we think the winner ends up owning the largest record of machine-run experiments anywhere.
projects.wedge: Closed-loop driver for one instrument class at DOE facilities
projects.trigger: Phase II applications from Phase I awardees under DOE's Genesis Mission RFA (DE-FOA-0003612) are due.

projects.name: Neuron-on-chip assays now, biological computing later
projects.problem: The FDA wants animal testing to become the exception, so pharma needs human neural tests that regulators will accept instead. Computing with living neurons, the bigger prize, is at least a decade away.
projects.solution: Analysis software and a data standard for neurons grown on electrode arrays, sold to pharma for drug discovery and neurotoxicity testing. That revenue pays for the longer road to biological computing.
projects.timing: The FDA's April 2025 roadmap aims to make animal studies the exception within three to five years. We expect the first neural assays to seek regulatory acceptance in 2027 and 2028.
projects.one_liner: Computing on living neurons is at least a decade away. FDA's move away from animal testing makes neurons on electrode arrays useful as a drug-discovery assay now, and that can pay for the compute research. We'd back a team whose first revenue is pharma and whose end state is a new kind of computer.
projects.wedge: Analysis software and data standard for neuron-on-array readouts
projects.trigger: FDA's window for making animal studies the exception closes, three to five years after the April 2025 roadmap.

projects.name: Power for data centers that can flex
projects.problem: New AI capacity waits years for a grid connection. Grid operators are deciding whether data centers that cut load on demand should get faster access, and they will need proof that a site actually cuts back when asked.
projects.solution: Metering and curtailment software whose numbers a grid operator accepts as a commitment. Once those numbers are trusted, the company can sell the combined flexibility of many sites into power markets and become the power supplier for compute.
projects.timing: Federal regulators ordered six grid operators in June 2026 to justify their rules for large loads. PJM holds its next capacity auction in December 2026.
projects.one_liner: Grid operators are rewriting the rules for large loads in 2026. Data centers that can prove they cut load on demand may get power years sooner. We'd back the software that proves it, and we think the winner grows into the energy company for compute.
projects.wedge: Curtailment attestation an RTO accepts
projects.trigger: PJM's Base Residual Auction for delivery year 2029/2030.

projects.name: Memory and optical interconnect tooling
projects.problem: Inside AI hardware, moving data now costs more energy than computing on it. The fixes are faster stacked memory, optics in place of copper, and model weights built into the chip. Each one takes billions in capex.
projects.solution: The tools those chip and optics companies need, starting with a compiler that turns a model checkpoint into a chip design with the weights built in. A tools company sees the bottleneck before anyone else, and the right team can grow into selling the part that fixes it.
projects.timing: SK hynix plans mass production of its next high-bandwidth memory, HBM4E, in 2027. Switches with optics inside the package are due in the second half of 2026.
projects.one_liner: Moving data now costs more energy than computing on it. The fixes are stacked memory, optics in place of copper, and weights built into the chip, and all three need billions of capex. We'd back the tooling those companies need, then look for the team that can grow from tools into silicon.
projects.wedge: Checkpoint-to-hardwired-silicon compiler
projects.trigger: SK hynix HBM4E mass production, which the company targets for 2027.

projects.name: Safety evidence for learning robots
projects.problem: Robots that learn from data get retrained often, and each new version reopens the question of whether the robot is still safe. Certifiers need evidence for every change, and robot makers have no fast way to produce it.
projects.solution: A pipeline that turns a robot's logs into the file a certifier asks for and tracks what changed at each retrain. The evidence has to come from someone other than the maker, which makes it hard for a robot company to bundle.
projects.timing: The EU Machinery Regulation applies on January 20, 2027. From that date, machinery whose safety relies on machine learning needs third-party sign-off.
projects.one_liner: From Jan 20, 2027, EU machinery whose safety depends on machine learning needs a notified body to sign off. Every retrained policy raises the same question again. We'd back the independent evidence and change-control system that answers it, starting in the EU and growing with every learning robot that ships.
projects.wedge: Log-to-conformity-file pipeline with change control on retrain
projects.trigger: EU Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies.

projects.name: AI chip design tools for the work Synopsys and Cadence won't do
projects.problem: Synopsys and Cadence are adding AI verification agents to the licenses chip teams already pay for, so a startup selling verification is up against a free feature. The slow part of a chip project shifts to the back end, where placement and timing depend on each company's own past designs.
projects.solution: An agent for timing closure, trained on a customer's own tape-outs and run inside its firewall. After that, tools for teams that mix Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens flows, since none of the three will tune for a rival's tools.
projects.timing: Both companies' agents reach customers by the end of 2026, so the back-end crunch shows up in 2027 design cycles.
projects.one_liner: Synopsys and Cadence both ship verification agents by the end of 2026. Once that happens, a startup selling front-end verification is selling against a free bundle. We'd back back-end tools trained on a customer's own tape-outs, and work that spans more than one vendor's tools.
projects.wedge: Timing-closure agent trained on a customer's own tape-outs
projects.trigger: Synopsys AgentEngineer and Autopilot availability planned for end of 2026, and Cadence RTL Generation Agent early access in Q4 2026.

projects.name: Proof checking for AI-written code
projects.problem: Agents write code faster than people can review it, and passing tests doesn't prove the code is right. Formal proofs do, but until now they cost too much for anything outside avionics and chip design.
projects.solution: An independent proof checker that runs in CI, accepts proofs from any model and produces evidence a regulator or insurer will accept. Start in one field where a bug is expensive, such as embedded firmware or crypto libraries.
projects.timing: The EU Cyber Resilience Act fully applies on December 11, 2027. Software sold in the EU will need evidence of secure design, and companies spend 2027 preparing it.
projects.one_liner: Agents now write code faster than people can review it, and passing tests doesn't mean the code is right. The EU's Cyber Resilience Act fully applies in December 2027. We'd back an independent checker that verifies machine-made proofs and produces evidence a regulator or insurer accepts.
projects.wedge: Proof-checking CI service for one vertical, with CRA evidence
projects.trigger: EU Cyber Resilience Act fully applies.

projects.name: Identity and permissions for AI agents
projects.problem: Most agents log in with a person's credentials or a shared service account that can do far more than the task needs. With ten agents that's manageable. With thousands, nobody can tell which agent did what, or switch off just one.
projects.solution: A credential broker that gives each agent short-lived access to exactly what one task needs, plugs into the identity provider a company already uses, and keeps an audit log the security team can search. It has to work across clouds and identity vendors, since each of them will bundle a version for its own customers.
projects.timing: Agent fleets move from pilots into production during 2027. The EU AI Act's rules for high-risk systems apply from December 2, 2027.
projects.one_liner: Companies are about to run thousands of agents that log into real systems with real credentials. Identity tools were built for people who sign in once a day. We'd back the company that gives each agent only the access one task needs, can revoke it in seconds, and can show afterwards who did what.
projects.wedge: Task-scoped credential broker for agents with an audit log
projects.trigger: EU AI Act high-risk obligations for Annex III systems apply, after the AI Omnibus delay.

projects.name: Verifying and paying for agent work
projects.problem: Regulated US stablecoins are coming, and issuers' anti-money-laundering programs assume a human customer. When an agent holds a wallet and pays, the issuer still has to know who is accountable for it and what it's allowed to spend.
projects.solution: A signed credential that ties an agent to a verified person or company and its spending limits, and a verifier that issuers and exchanges call when the payment happens. Checking that the agent actually did the work it was paid for comes next.
projects.timing: The OCC's rule implementing the GENIUS Act takes effect on January 18, 2027.
projects.one_liner: Regulated US stablecoins arrive on Jan 18, 2027, and the issuers' anti-money-laundering programs assume a human customer. Agents with wallets break that assumption. We'd back the credential and verifier that tell an issuer or exchange which accountable person or company an agent acts for and what it may spend, and grow from there into checking the work itself.
projects.wedge: Know-your-agent credential and verifier for stablecoin issuers and exchanges, with an exportable audit trail
projects.trigger: The GENIUS Act and the OCC's implementing rule take effect (OCC final rule, Federal Register, Oct 23, 2026, effective Jan 18, 2027; OCC Bulletin 2026-50).

projects.name: Software for agent CPUs
projects.problem: AI agents spend most of their time on ordinary CPU work: calling tools, compiling code, starting sandboxes. Today's sandbox software was designed for a few dozen virtual machines per server. NVIDIA says one of its new agent racks holds more than 22,500 environments.
projects.solution: A sandbox runtime that starts and forks agent environments in milliseconds and fits far more of them on each rack, shipped with an open benchmark so buyers can check the numbers themselves.
projects.timing: NVIDIA and Arm both start shipping CPUs built for agents by the end of 2026, and those racks fill up in 2027.
projects.one_liner: Agents spend most of their time on CPU work, and NVIDIA and Arm both start shipping CPUs sold for agents by the end of 2026. We think the software that packs thousands of agent sandboxes onto one rack is the opening, and nobody we found is funded to build it.
projects.wedge: Fast snapshot-and-fork sandbox runtime with an open density benchmark
projects.trigger: NVIDIA Vera systems from partners "starting this fall" and Arm AGI CPU first production shipments by end of 2026.

projects.name: Operations for mixed AI clusters
projects.problem: New AI racks mix NVIDIA GPUs with inference chips, liquid cooling and, soon, optics packaged inside the switch. They break in new ways, and neoclouds and enterprises can't hire hyperscaler-size teams to keep them running.
projects.solution: Failure diagnosis and repair for these racks, sold with an uptime guarantee and delivered by software plus technicians on site. As what the technicians learn turns into software, margins grow faster than headcount.
projects.timing: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin systems and its first co-packaged optics switches reach neoclouds in the second half of 2026.
projects.one_liner: Inference racks now mix NVIDIA GPUs, inference chips and soon co-packaged optics. Neoclouds and enterprises can't hire hyperscaler-size ops teams to run them. We'd back the company that keeps those racks running to an SLA, in software and on site.
projects.wedge: Failure diagnosis and repair for neocloud racks, software plus technicians
projects.trigger: Vera Rubin systems and Spectrum-X Photonics switches reach neoclouds in H2 2026.
